findings: [P1] packages/cadenda/server.py: create_app() never calls Recorder.recover() and exposes no recovery operation. After a GUI worker crashes while Claimed/Running/Verifying, its row remains active indefinitely: new starts fail, cancel only sets a flag no surviving worker consumes, and resume rejects the executing state. Reconcile dead workers at startup and through an authenticated recovery operation or equivalent refresh flow, preserving process-group checks before release. Test restarting the GUI with a dead worker and an active run, then recovering and explicitly resuming it.

[P2] packages/cadenda/server.py: resume() releases the original run before start_job() checks CONFIG_REQUIRED, existing GUI jobs and other launch failures. A rejected resume or failed Popen therefore permanently changes the preserved run to Abandoned without creating a replacement; subsequent resume attempts reject it. Perform all non-mutating launch checks before release, and provide a durable, retryable recovery path when launch fails after release. Test both a conflicting GUI job and an injected launcher failure.
requirements_checked: Reviewed supplied source only; used no tools. Supplied test results were not independently verified.
Checked pairing possession, single use, session expiry/logout, cookie settings, Host/Origin and CSRF enforcement. Actor names and AI verdicts were not treated as authentication.
Checked request bounds, routing, fixed launch arguments, cancellation/resume, SSE cursors and React asynchronous state handling.
Checked artifact binding, approval freshness, tampering, challenge expiry/replay and decision receipt verification by ContextBuilder.
The two prior findings are addressed in the supplied implementation: approval previews redact displayed targets, and job polling checks target and generation.
Excluded simultaneous external Beads writes and Phase 7 requirements as specified.
